summary: 100-foot steel lookout tower near Buick, Iron County; erected 1934, credited to CCC Company 732 in a later feature; 1939 survey described it; no source found for today's status.

facts.design: Four-legged steel tower with an eight-foot square cab on top; ladder to the cab in 1934
facts.agency: Mark Twain National Forest (Clark National Forest and Clark Unit in 1934)

events.note: Material arrived March 1934 for a 100-foot steel lookout tower near Buick, to be erected immediately. A later Salem News feature credits CCC Company 732, working from Boss Camp F-1.
By November 1934 a newspaper item about the Marcoot tower described the Buick and Czar towers as present towers that used a ladder to reach the cab.
Coast and Geodetic Survey station described on the tower finial; the description gives both 100 feet and about 110 feet for the tower.

corrections.proposed: Mark Twain National Forest (Clark National Forest and Clark Unit in 1934)
corrections.why: The record names no forest. The 1934 item places the tower in the Clark Unit, which later became the Clark National Forest; that forest was combined with Mark Twain in 1973 and absorbed in 1976.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1934 newspaper gives 100 feet, and the 1939 survey text gives both 100 feet and about 110 feet. The record keeps 30.5 m (100 ft). No source read says which figure is right.

notes_for_editor: Today's status and access are not found in any source read; the story says so. A WebFetch summary of a Missouri Life fire-tower article (fetch_text returned HTTP 403, so the page is not cached and no quote can be checked) says a lookout manned 'the Buick tower' and names an Oates tower as removed. The article date and whether Buick still stands are unknown, so it is not used; worth a human check. A 1984 NRHP eligibility evaluation of three lookout tower sites in Iron, Barry and Stone counties surfaced in search but was not available; it is unknown whether Buick is one of them. Record coordinates 37.608, -91.1287 were not checked against any map. Record agency 'National Forest' is corrected above.
